text: Hume holds that we possess a distinct, separate impression of time itself, over and above our impressions of successive objects.
explanation: This is false. Hume explicitly denies any distinct impression of time: the idea of time 'is not derived from a particular impression' but 'arises altogether from the manner in which impressions appear to the mind' in succession (Treatise I.ii.3). Because we have no impression of a changeless, event-free flow, Hume concludes that Newton's absolute time is a philosophical fiction — the opposite of the claim stated here.
